audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions Crimson Pact (P), the single interaction that decides how Zac's W scales into Vladimir.
audit.why: Crimson Pact converts 1 AP into 1.6 bonus Health (and 30 bonus Health into 1 AP). Every AP item Vladimir buys inflates his max-HP pool, and Unstable Matter (W) deals a percentage of MAX health as magic damage on a flat 5s cooldown. A full-build Vladimir is therefore a *better* W target than an early one — the opposite of the usual 'mage gets tankier so stop hitting him' instinct.
audit.corrected: Vladimir's AP-to-HP passive feeds Zac's percent-max-HP W; W him every 5s in extended fights rather than saving it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers say 'engage when Sanguine Pool is on cooldown' repeatedly but never state how long that window is, so the advice is unactionable.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s for 2s of untargetability. Zac's Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9s. Through the whole laning phase Zac's engage cooldown is SHORTER than Vladimir's escape cooldown, which means a disciplined Zac gets a free, unanswerable commit every single rotation. That is the actual win condition and the numbers prove it.
audit.corrected: Pool 28s (rank 1) vs your E 21s — bait Pool, then commit inside the gap. At rank 3 it is 22s vs your 15s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds despite Vladimir healing off both Transfusion (Q) and Hemoplague (R).
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags this matchup needs-antiheal for Transfusion (Q) and Hemoplague (R). Transfusion reaches a 4.6s cooldown at rank 5, so in an extended fight it is close to permanent sustain; without anti-heal Zac's grind simply cannot out-damage it.
audit.corrected: Buy Grievous Wounds around first item and have it up before any 5v5 where Hemoplague heals him per champion hit.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] said to use R to 'fling him out of Hemoplague range'.
audit.why: Hemoplague is cast on an area to infect Zac's team and amplify damage they take; it is not a zone Vladimir stands in, so 'flinging him out of it' describes an interaction that does not exist. R's real job is displacing him off Zac's carries.
audit.corrected: Use Let's Bounce! to knock Vladimir off your carries, not to move him out of his own ult.

edits.after: Sanguine Pool (W) is 2s of untargetable on a 28s rank-1 cooldown — longer than your 21s E — so every rotation hands you one engage he cannot answer. Count it down from the moment he spends it.

edits.after: With Rylai's/Riftmaker online Transfusion (Q) drops to a 4.6s cooldown and out-heals your chip — Grievous Wounds is mandatory here, and his AP-to-HP passive feeds your W percent-HP damage.

edits.before: Late Vlad is a teamfight monster; your only real tool is R (Let's Bounce!) to fling him out of Hemoplague range before he pools — flank so he can't Pool-reset your engage.
edits.after: Late Vlad is a teamfight monster and Let's Bounce! is your only tool that reaches him — knock him off your carries, and flank so Pool cannot simply erase the engage you spent.

edits.after: From 2 on Vlad takes over, so make one rule: never open E while Pool is up. Bait it with a W tick or a Q, then E-Q immediately — Pool is 22s at rank 3 and he has no other answer inside that window.

edits.after: Late Vlad is a drain-tank carry who beats your solo pressure across the board, so your value is teamfight peel and picks — Grievous Wounds before the 5v5, then R him off your carries; the 51.9% reflects your tank-teamfight edge despite him owning the lane.

notes: The two layers disagree on the level chart: content win[] gives Vladimir 6/7 stages while full phases[].side gives Zac 4/7 (Skill,Zac,Zac,Skill,Skill,Zac,Zac). Zac's Emerald+ rate here is 51.93% over 181 games, so the full layer is closer to the data; I did not propose chart flips because the disagreement is a generator-level inconsistency, not a single wrong cell. The packet's suspectName ('Let's Bounce' in spikes[3]) is a FALSE POSITIVE — the file already writes 'Let's Bounce!' correctly; the detector is stripping the trailing '!'. Not verified and therefore left alone: whether Sanguine Pool's untargetability drops an already-applied Zac Q tether, and whether Pool can be used to avoid the knock-up component of E on landing.
